attribution.note: Zitron's own reporting sentence in his signed article.

semantics.note: The proposition matches the claim that website pricing showed Claude Code removed from Pro on both mobile and desktop.

contract.note: It is fair to require evidence for both presentations, because the speaker named both. Tying the claim to the April 21 episode follows from the context.

evidence.note: Ars confirms the pricing page showed Pro without Claude Code and was later restored. It does not separate mobile from desktop layouts, so it cannot settle the two-device claim.

reviews.rationale: The general pricing-page change is corroborated. No independent capture or firsthand report confirms exclusion on both mobile and desktop presentations, and nothing shows either one kept Pro inclusion. The device-specific claim is unsettled.

semantics.note: Keeps 'various pricing pages' and the date. Drops 'later afternoon', a minor loss given no timezone.

contract.note: Reading 'removed access' as advertised entitlement fits the context. Requiring more than one page follows from the speaker's plural 'various'.

evidence.note: Separately from Zitron, GIGAZINE cites George Pu's April 21 observation that the Pro price list lacked Claude Code. This confirms one pricing page (claude.com/pricing), not several.

reviews.rationale: Independent reporting confirms the main pricing page dropped Claude Code from Pro on April 21. The contract's support condition requires multiple pricing pages, and the packet establishes only one. Nothing contradicts the claim. The core is corroborated but the plural scope is unsettled.

attribution.note: Zitron's own update text, responding to Avasare.

semantics.note: Separates the factual part (all docs and the website showed exclusion) from the evaluative 'does not make sense' and keeps the 'all' quantifier.

contract.note: Holding the speaker to his literal 'all' is fair. Separating public messaging from experiment enrollment is a reasonable reading.

evidence.note: Company disclosure: Avasare admits the landing page and docs changes were public and confused the 98% outside the test. This supports a broad public messaging mismatch.
The Register's firsthand report, filed during the episode, says the Claude Code product page still advertised Pro access. That contradicts uniform exclusion across the website.

reviews.rationale: Holds: public pricing and docs showed Pro without Claude Code, which clashed with a ~2% test (e4). Fails: 'all' and the whole website, because the product page still listed Pro access (e5). The enrollment percentage itself is not tested.

attribution.note: Zitron's own sentence in his article.

semantics.note: 'I do not believe this is the last time' is an ungraded expectation, like 'I expect', so a forecast is right. Setting the modality to 'likely' understates his commitment, but the proposition text still fits.

contract.note: 'In this manner' is vague. Reading it as a comparable access restriction brought in through pricing or docs with little notice is a fair contextual reading. No deadline was given.

evidence.note: Official support page: the planned Agent SDK change was paused and subscription usage kept. No recurrence was implemented.
An August limit cut with misleading framing, but announced before the September start and not an access removal. It does not meet the early-resolution rule.

reviews.rationale: The forecast has no deadline. No documented event in the packet shows a comparable access restriction introduced without notice, so the early-resolution rule is not met. Without recurrence so far, an open-ended forecast cannot be contradicted.
